references.text: God promised that He would be with Moses' mouth and teach him what to say, and that Aaron should be his spokesman.
Miriam prophesied and led the women in praise, which shows that she also had a prophetic ministry.
Aaron was appointed as Moses' prophet and spokesman before Pharaoh.
God gave His Spirit to the seventy elders so they prophesied, and Moses expressed the wish that all of the Lord's people were prophets.
The Lord's response to Miriam's and Aaron's complaint, where He explains Moses' unique position as a prophet.
Hagar calls the Lord 'the God who sees', an example of how God hears and sees everything.
The psalmist confirms that God hears everything - He who planted the ear, should He not hear?
Micah confirms that God sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead Israel, showing that all three had a God-given role.
Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's house, which underscores his unique position among God's servants.
